name: Hot Snakes
label: Swami
lede: Two San Diego guitarists, a drummer in Philadelphia and a painter in New York made three records in five years, in whatever weeks their calendars overlapped.

eras.title: Two guys, two bands, one habit
eras.text: Long before Hot Snakes, John Reis and Rick Froberg were already making noise together in San Diego. Their first two bands, Pitchfork and Drive Like Jehu, are where the partnership got its shape.

years.src: Rolling Stone · Sub Pop: Hot Snakes
years.h: [[John Reis|626e7b64-3035-4f58-92a6-49790f600e30]] and [[Rick Froberg|07d99b38-fa92-4916-a190-1240b1d2e402]] start Pitchfork in San Diego
years.p: Sub Pop says the two had been collaborating since high school. The quartet released the album Eucalyptus in 1990.
years.xp: Rolling Stone's obituary of Froberg dates Pitchfork to 1986 and calls it a San Diego quartet formed by Froberg and Reis. Sub Pop's Hot Snakes bio describes the pair as collaborators since high school, which makes Hot Snakes the third band in a partnership that had already run more than a decade.

years.h: [[Drive Like Jehu|608c9da7-d3ef-4661-828b-24bb6ae20cd6]]: Yank Crime
years.p: Reis and Froberg's second band followed a 1991 self-titled debut with a record of tangled time signatures. Rolling Stone says it went on to cult status.
years.xp: Rolling Stone describes Drive Like Jehu as a post-hardcore act with complex time signatures. When the band's reunion tours ran in 2015 and 2016, Reis told the Shepherd Express that they reignited his musical direction, and that the music of Hot Snakes was still current to what he was attracted to.

eras.title: A drummer in Philadelphia, a painter in New York
eras.text: Hot Snakes began as a way for Reis to hear the sound in his head, with Rocket from the Crypt between labels and short a drummer. Froberg turned it into a band from another city.

years.cap: Hot Snakes in the Automatic Midnight era. Photographer to be added.
years.src: No Recess · Shepherd Express · Wikipedia: Hot Snakes
years.h: Reis starts Hot Snakes with a Delta 72 drummer
years.p: With [[Rocket from the Crypt|e297ecdf-64ec-4e34-899d-80380f5b0c2a]] between labels and without its drummer, Reis gathers a few days with [[The Delta 72|0e1a1b82-904f-49b0-8955-086f0bf28afa]] drummer Jason Kourkounis, who lives in Philadelphia.
years.xp:
Reis told No Recess that Kourkounis flew out for a day or two, then came back for four days. They practiced for two of them, spent two days in the studio and recorded 20 songs. Reis has said he had the sound in his head and wanted to hear what it actually sounded like.

Reis tried the vocals himself first and decided against it. That is how the band ended up with a singer who lived in another city.

q: He completely elevated all the songs, all the music; everything just got way better.
years.h: Froberg signs on from New York, and the songs get better
years.p: He moved east to make art, so the singer of Hot Snakes lives nowhere near the band. Reis credits him with lifting everything.
years.xp: Froberg also drew all the band's artwork. Members were spread across San Diego, New York and Philadelphia. Wikipedia notes the geography is why touring and recording came in bursts.

years.h: Automatic Midnight on Swami Records
years.p: Recorded in June 1999 at Big Fish Recorders in San Diego with engineer Ben Moore. It runs 31 minutes and 36 seconds.
years.xp: Froberg drew the artwork in black and white, but the packaging used translucent orange, so the finished record looked orange. Pitchfork gave it a 7.6 on release.

eras.title: Fire, organ, and a Peel session
eras.text: Gar Wood joined as bassist, the band moved into Reis's own practice space, and the sound got stranger before it got tighter. Then the drummer changed and the band toured hard for a year.

years.h: Suicide Invoice adds organ and melodica
years.p: Recorded at Reis's Drag Racist practice space, it puts a Magi 44 organ and melodica into the songs. Pitchfork gave it an 8.8.
years.xp:
Reis told No Recess that he was inexperienced at recording there and that some logistics went wrong, and called it "a trial by jizz". He still thought the record turned out great. Drag Racist burned down the following year.

Frankie Stains plays organ on the closing song, "Paid in Cigarettes". Kourkounis is credited under the name Jsinclair.

years.h: Kourkounis leaves for Burning Brides, Mario Rubalcaba takes the sticks
years.p: Rubalcaba had been drumming for Rocket from the Crypt since 2000. Kourkounis went to play full time with Burning Brides.

years.src: Wikipedia: Audit in Progress · No Recess
years.h: Audit in Progress: the Rubalcaba record
years.p: Recorded at Big Fish Recorders and mastered by Dave Gardner, it won best punk album at the 2005 San Diego Music Awards.
years.xp: Reis called it "deconstructed rock 'n' roll" in the No Recess interview. Spin called it "loud, throttling punk-rock elegance". Its song "This Mystic Decade" later turned up on the Grand Theft Auto V soundtrack.

years.cap: Hot Snakes on the road, 2004. Photographer to be added.
years.h: A Peel Session on the fall 2004 UK tour
years.p: Hot Snakes recorded at John Peel's BBC studio while on tour. Punknews' headline called it Peel's last ever session, and it came out as the Peel Sessions EP in April 2005.
years.xp: Wikipedia describes it as one of the last sessions for Peel's program before his death. Punknews' headline for the EP announcement called it the last one ever, so the sources differ on the wording.

years.h: An Australian tour, then Hot Snakes is over
years.p: Reis ended the band after the tour, and Rocket from the Crypt with it, to focus on being a father.
years.xp: Shepherd Express reports that Reis stopped both Hot Snakes and Rocket from the Crypt in 2005 to put fatherhood first. A live set from Australian radio, taped at the ABC's triple j studios in May 2005, came out the next year as Thunder Down Under.

eras.title: Everybody gets a side project
eras.text: Reis kept Swami Records running and formed the Night Marchers with Wood and Kourkounis. Froberg started Obits. One three-song encore in 2010 changed the mood.

years.h: The last session: a Government Issue cover for Tony Hawk
years.p: Hot Snakes cut "Time to Escape" for the soundtrack of Tony Hawk's American Wasteland. It is the final thing they recorded before the split.

years.h: Thunder Down Under: live from triple j
years.p: A May 2005 studio set for Australian radio, released after the breakup.

years.h: Froberg debuts Obits, and Reis starts the Night Marchers
years.p: Obits, Froberg's new band, plays its first shows. Reis, Wood and Kourkounis play together in the Night Marchers.

years.cap: The Casbah, San Diego. Photo to be added.
years.h: Three songs at the Casbah, unannounced
years.p: The original four played an encore of "If Credit's What Matters I'll Take Credit", "Automatic Midnight" and "No Hands".
years.xp: Wikipedia dates the encore to July 29, 2010 at San Diego's Casbah and lists those three songs. The official reunion followed in 2011.

eras.title: Back out of the dead
eras.text: The reunion started as festival dates, then turned into a new album on Sub Pop, with all three old records reissued around it.

years.h: All Tomorrow's Parties and Fun Fun Fun Fest bring them back
years.p: West Coast dates followed in March and April 2012, and the Metallica-curated Orion Music + More festival in New Jersey that June.

years.src: Wikipedia: Hot Snakes · Sub Pop News
yt: Hot Snakes, full performance, live on KEXP
years.h: Sub Pop announces tour dates and a new album
years.p: The band announced fall touring and a record for Sub Pop. That November Sub Pop scheduled reissues of all three Swami albums for January 2018 plus UK dates.

years.h: Jericho Sirens: the first record in 14 years
years.p: Ten songs in 30 minutes on Sub Pop. Froberg flew to California to write with Reis, and the album was recorded with both Kourkounis and Rubalcaba on drums.
years.xp:
Exclaim! reports Kourkounis drummed on seven tracks and Rubalcaba on three. Froberg said of them: "They were both welcome to join in. We couldn't really say 'You can play and you can't.'"

Metacritic lists 86. Pitchfork gave it a 7.7.

years.h: "Not in Time", a new song with a hallucinatory video
years.p: Sub Pop released the video on a Thursday and pushed the track for Bandcamp Friday the next day.

eras.title: Rick
eras.text: Froberg died with a fifth album he said was nearly finished.

years.h: Froberg dies at 55
years.p: Reis announced it on Instagram: Froberg had died suddenly the night before, from natural causes. Weeks earlier Froberg had said a fifth album was nearly finished.
years.xp:
Rolling Stone and Clash quote Reis writing: "Rick passed away suddenly last night from natural causes." BrooklynVegan reports that days later Froberg's girlfriend, Britt, wrote on his Instagram that the cause was an undiagnosed heart condition, which Wikipedia also states. Wikipedia gives the date as June 30, 2023.

In August 2023 Reis told an interviewer the band had been working on new music. He said it was every bit as good as, if not better than, the first Hot Snakes record.

years.h: Plenty For All collects Froberg's art
years.p: Akashic Books published the book of his pen and ink drawings, linocuts, paintings, watercolors and commercial work.
